recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-12254 unless a future work group decision changes the request status vocabulary or the requester-versus-performer-state guidance.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core-_Request issue asking to change the Request.status comment from requester control over completed/cancelled/etc. after activation to a clearer statement that the requester controls draft/active and, after activation, completed/cancelled/suspended states, while performer activity state is represented by Event resources or Task.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite svn @10123. Git history maps that to 785a04a465032908316dcf4741f24a769c6c194b, which changed source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml for #12254 from the older misspelled 'competed, cancelled, etc.' wording to the requested draft/active and completed/cancelled/suspended wording.
additional_context: The Request logical pattern remains in current build scope through source/fhir.ini's active [logical] request entry. Current source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml retains the FHIR-12254 distinction between requester-controlled status and performer fulfillment state, but the status names have evolved to the current RequestStatus vocabulary: ended, completed, revoked, and on-hold rather than the old cancelled/suspended wording. Current parallel resource comments, including ServiceRequest and NutritionOrder, align with the same guidance family.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current source already conveys the FHIR-12254 semantic clarification and should not be reverted toward the exact DSTU2 wording because that wording no longer matches the current code system.

related_jiras.note: Later request-status alignment moved this wording family from cancelled/suspended toward the current ended, revoked, and on-hold vocabulary. It was context only, not separately decided here.

A later reconciliation on the combined branch aligned NutritionOrder.status wording with the request-pattern intent. It was already represented separately and not decided here.
